summary:
We built the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, a free browser game that teaches kids how astronauts dock with the International Space Station. Players fly a small capsule into the station’s docking port using the keyboard or on-screen touch controls. Because the capsule keeps drifting and fuel is limited, kids learn that thrusters push the opposite way, that moving objects keep moving, and that fuel has to be planned. If they touch the port too fast, they crash, just as in real life.

The game has six stages that get harder, with a moving port, space junk and less fuel. Each stage starts with a short tip, and each successful docking shows a space fact. A glowing ring around the capsule shows whether the speed is safe. Finishing all six stages earns a rank, from Rookie Astronaut to Mission Commander. A built-in autopilot demo shows how docking works step by step.

It addresses the challenge by making astronaut training simple, hands-on and fun for young learners. It matters because it needs no install and works on phones, tablets and computers, so more kids can try it and get curious about space and STEM.
details:
What it does and how it works

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a free browser game that teaches kids how astronauts dock with the International Space Station. Players fly a small capsule into the station’s glowing docking port using the arrow keys, W A S D, or on-screen touch buttons. Movement follows simple physics: thrusters push the capsule the opposite way, the capsule keeps drifting until the player brakes, and fuel is limited. If the capsule touches the port too fast, it crashes, as it would in real life. A ring around the capsule turns green when the speed is safe to dock.

The game has six stages that get harder: a still port, a moving port, space junk, a faster port, a debris storm, and a final stage with the least fuel. Each stage opens with a short tip, and each successful docking shows a space fact. Players earn points, with a bonus for saving fuel, and a final rank from Rookie Astronaut to Mission Commander. A built-in autopilot demo shows the steps of docking with captions.

Benefits and intended impact

Kids learn three ideas by playing: Newton’s third law, that moving objects keep moving, and planning limited resources. The game needs no download, account or special hardware, so it runs on phones, tablets and computers. We hope it makes astronaut training feel reachable and sparks curiosity about space and STEM.

Tools used

The game is built with HTML5 Canvas, CSS and plain JavaScript in a single file with no libraries. The slide deck was made with PptxGenJS, and the demo video was recorded with Playwright and converted with FFmpeg. An AI assistant, Claude by Anthropic, helped with the ideas, code, text, design and presentation.

What is creative

We turned one real part of astronaut training, docking, into a short game instead of a quiz. The rule that speed matters more than distance makes kids think like a pilot. Everything on screen, including Earth, the station and the capsule, is drawn in code, so the whole project is one lightweight file.

Factors we considered

  • Accessibility: it works with keyboard, mouse or touch, and in light and dark mode.
  • Performance: game speed is the same on 60 Hz and high-refresh screens.
  • Age-appropriate difficulty: the first stages are easy, and the tips explain the rules.
  • Accuracy: the space facts are simplified for young learners and written from general knowledge.
